The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 11.10.2022.
2.

The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 11.10.2022 at about 08.45 p.m., petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA- 08-H-7521 slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules proceeding on Chikkanahalli-Chinnadahalli Village, Nandagudi Hobli Hoskote Taluk, Bangalore, at that time the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-5993 ridden in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner from behind.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately, he was shifted to Gaurav Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 36 years, the petitioner was working at Ninjacart Company and earning Rs.35,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notice, the respondent No.2 remained absent.
Hence, placed exparte.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle.

Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 147, 149(2), 134(c), 158(6) of M. V. Act.
This respondent further submits that, complaint is lodged after the lapse of 01 day and no valid reason is assigned for the delay in lodging the complaint.

Further this respondent submits that,
the petitioner was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
The petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident.
He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 11.10.2022 at about 8.45 p.m., while petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing reg. No. KA-08-H-7521 carefully

cautiously by observing all traffic rules and proceeding on Chikkanahalli - Chinnadahalli Village, Nandagudi Hobli, Hoskote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, at that time, motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-5993 ridden by its rider in a very rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, came at high speed and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle from behind, caused the accident and as a result, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries as alleged by him?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or Award?
5.

On the other hand, respondent No.1 examined their witnesses as RW.1 to RW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.5.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.

10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that on 11.10.2022 at about 08.45 p.m.,
petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-08-H-7521 slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules proceeding on Chikkanahalli-Chinnadahalli Village, Nandagudi Hobli Hoskote Taluk, Bangalore, at that time the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-5993 ridden in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner from behind.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.
Immediately, he was shifted to Gaurav Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the Nandagudi Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.168/2022.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC along with section 181, 196 and 187 of M. V. Act.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.

The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-5993.
12.

As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "
The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt,
as it is insisted in criminal case for " The Negligent Act ".
13.

17. In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place.

By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-5993.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
18. ISSUE No.2:
The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Gaurav Hospital, wherein he was admitted was inpatient and he took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

In the petition as well as in his evidence PW.1 deposed that,
immediately after the accident he was shifted to Gaurav Hospital as an inpatient from 11.10.2022 to 15.10.2022 and again from 04.03.2023 to 06.03.2023.
The petitioner has produced the discharge card marked at Ex.P.9 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, Bangalore for 06 days.

Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.

22. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability-
The petitioner contended that, he has discontinued his service due to the accident.

This shows that, the petitioner is not suffering from disability.
Hence, this tribunal can infer that there is no disability caused to the petitioner and he is not entitle for the compensation under this head.

26. LIABILITY:
In this case as discussed in Issue No.1, accident is caused due to the rash and negligent act of offending vehicle.
In this case, owner of the offending vehicle i.e., respondent No.2 has not filed any objections to the main petitions.

But respondent No.1 i.e., Insurance Company has filed objections and taken defense that, driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective Driving license as well as not wearing helmet as on the date of accident.
In support of his case, insurance company examined three witnesses as RW.1 to RW.3.
One Nagaraj i.e., official of RTO, K. R. Puram, Bangalore examine before the court as RW.1.
He depose that, as per the direction of the court they have searched the driving license of Munishyama Gowda S/o Munirajappa in their official website.
But they unable to trace the driving license extract of Munishyama Gowda.
During his cross-examination
learned counsel for petitioner taken defense that, second respondent not digitized his driving license so same is not reflected in the Sarathi-4 website.
But witness denied the same.
One S. Narayana swamy, ASI, Nandgudi police station examined before the court as RW.2.
He depose that, he has conducted the entire investigation inrespect of Nandagudi Crime No.168/2022.

Further he deposed that, during investigation, he has issued notice to the Munishyame Gowda to furnish the driving license but he has not furnished any license so that, he has filed final report against accused for the offence punishable u/sec.181, 196, 187 of M. V. Act and sec. 279 and 338 of IPC.
During his cross-examination
learned counsel for petitioner suggested that, second respondent was having driving license but you have filed false charge-sheet against the second respondent/accused.
But witness denied the said suggestion.

sentences.text: Vinay Prasad, Manager of respondent No.1 company examined as RW.3, wherein he reiterated the contents of the written statement.
Though the learned counsel for petitioner cross examined the RW.3 but failed to culled out from the mouth of witness that, at the time of accident respondent No.2 was having Driving License.

So, on going through the above oral evidence of the witnesses as well as documentary evidence of respondent side as well as police records, it goes to show that, a the time of accident rider of the offending vehicle was not having Driving License.
Though petitioner have taken contention that, at the time of accident rider of offending vehicle was having Driving License to ride the vehicle.
Admittedly, he has not produced any such document to show that, rider of the offending vehicle was having valid and effective license at the time of accident.
So, having regard to the above evidence as well as discussion this court opine that at the time of accident, rider of the offending vehicle was not possess the driving license.

In Beli Ram Vs. Rajinder Kumar and Another [AIR 2020 SC 4453] wherein the Apex Court observed as under:-
"Motor Vehicles Act (59 of 198), S.149 (2)(ao(ii), S.15 - Insurer's liability - Non-renewal of driving licence - Respondent - Claimant employed as driver met with accident while driving truck owned by employer - License not renewed for period of three years and that too in respect of commercial vehicle like truck - employer cannot wash his hands off responsibility of not checking up whether the driver has renewed license - Gross negligence on part of employees as insured in verifying driving license, Insurance Company not liable to pay compensation."

U/sec 3 of M. V Act and also meaning and definition of 'Effective driving licence' viz a viz section 3,
4 and 5 of M. V Act, whereby the insurance company has done all its efforts in establishing the fact that there was a fundamental breach of policy condition.

If a person drives the vehicle without a driving license or the owner allows the person to drive the vehicle without driving license there is a breach of section 3 of M. V Act which would no doubt make the owner liable for the consequences as per the M. V act and as per the section 181 of M. V Act.
27.
In this case, petitioner has not proved that the rider of the two-wheeler was having driving license at the time of accident.
Therefore, the court has opinion that the rider of the two-wheeler was not having driving license at the time of accident.
There is fundamental breach of terms and conditions of the policy.

Therefore, judgment in MFA No. 22781/2012 C/w MFA No. 22539/2012 (MV) in a case The Divisional Manager, Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Shri Arjun Datatray Gurav and another, wherein it is held that when there is fundamental breach of the policy condition the legibility fix on the insurance company.

28. Further this court has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme court of India 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 932 in a case of Balu Krishna Chavan Vs. The Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. & others wherein held that if the liability of the insurance company is decided and they are held Channa Krishnappa M.C vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160696662/
8 not to the liable, ordinarily, there shall be no direction to "pay and recover",

sentences.text: Further in para No.8 held that hence, the only aspect for out consideration herein, is as to whether in the facts and circumstances of the present case, an order to direct the Insurance Company to "pay and recover", is required to be made.
On this aspect, the law is well settled that if the liability of the Insurance Company is decided and they are held not to be liable, ordinarily, there shall be no direction to "pay and recover".
However, in the facts and circumstances arising in each case, appropriate orders are required to be made by this court to meet the ends of justice.
(emphasis supplied).
Therefore, in view of the above dictum of the hon'ble Supreme court of India the principal of pay and recovery cannot be applies in the present case.
Therefore, under such circumstances, it is the owner respondent No.2 is held liable to pay the compensation as awarded by the tribunal.
The liability of the insurance company is hereby exonerated from the liability.

The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 11.10.2022.
2.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 11.10.2022 at about 8.45 p.m., while petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing reg. No. KA-08-H-7521 carefully
,
cautiously by observing all traffic rules and proceeding on Chikkanahalli - Chinnadahalli Village, Nandagudi Hobli, Hoskote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, at that time, motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-5993 ridden by its rider in a very rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, came at high speed and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle from behind, caused the accident and as a result, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries as alleged by him?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.
Immediately, he was shifted to Gaurav Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the Nandagudi Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.168/2022.
After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC along with section 181, 196 and 187 of M. V. Act.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.
The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-5993.
12.
As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "
The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt,
as it is insisted in criminal case for " The Negligent Act ".
13.
15. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
16.
U/sec 3 of M. V Act and also meaning and definition of 'Effective driving licence' viz a viz section 3,
4 and 5 of M. V Act, whereby the insurance company has done all its efforts in establishing the fact that there was a fundamental breach of policy condition.
If a person drives the vehicle without a driving license or the owner allows the person to drive the vehicle without driving license there is a breach of section 3 of M. V Act which would no doubt make the owner liable for the consequences as per the M. V act and as per the section 181 of M. V Act.
27.
In this case, petitioner has not proved that the rider of the two-wheeler was having driving license at the time of accident.
Therefore, the court has opinion that the rider of the two-wheeler was not having driving license at the time of accident.
There is fundamental breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, this being the violation of the policy conditions while considering the liability.
28. Further this court has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme court of India 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 932 in a case of Balu Krishna Chavan Vs. The Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. & others wherein held that if the liability of the insurance company is decided and they are held Channa Krishnappa M.C vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160696662/
8 not to the liable, ordinarily, there shall be no direction to "pay and recover",
On this aspect, the law is well settled that if the liability of the Insurance Company is decided and they are held not to be liable, ordinarily, there shall be no direction to "pay and recover".
However, in the facts and circumstances arising in each case, appropriate orders are required to be made by this court to meet the ends of justice.
Therefore, under such circumstances, it is the owner respondent No.2 is held liable to pay the compensation as awarded by the tribunal.

30. ISSUE No.3:
In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.2,17,956/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 being owner of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount, entire amount shall be released in his favour.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
Channa
The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.
